title: Functional restoration of conformational (R175H) and contact (R273H) mutant p53 by Bacillus-derived Hydroxymycotrienin A in non-small cell lung cancer: a computational approach.
authors: Rufus, Adeline Celina; Kumar N, Sidharth; Ramasamy, Magesh; Elangovan, Elavarashi
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过虚拟筛选和MD模拟寻找恢复突变p53功能的小分子，虽涉及p53-DNA结合界面稳定化，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非TF-DNA结合机制建模，方法可迁移性有限。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The TP53 mutations in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) remain a formidable clinical challenge. Current strategies, using the covalent binder APR-246, are limited by off-target toxicity and resistance. METHODS: This study screens 1,580 Bacillus-derived metabolites to identify novel non-covalent pharmacological chaperones for native, conformational (R175H), and contact (R273H) p53 mutants. Virtual screening, ADMET profiling, molecular docking, extended 500 ns Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations and Principal Component Analysis, against experimental anti-cancer drug APR-246, and top hit compounds. RESULTS: Hydroxymycotrienin A emerged as the potential candidate, demonstrating thermodynamic superiority with binding affinities of -6.63 kcal/mol (R175H) and -6.57 kcal/mol (R273H), demonstrated significant superior non covalent docking affinity compared to APR-246 parent scaffold (approximately -3.5 kcal/mol) in the mutated p53 protein, suggesting a direct pharmacological chaperone activity. Unlike the covalent alkylating mechanism of APR-246, Hydroxymycotrienin A utilizes a non-covalent network to chaperone the mutant p53. MD simulations revealed that Hydroxymycotrienin A acted as a structural stabilizer for the conformational mutant R175H by suppressing atomic fluctuations within the L2 loop and reducing overall structural deviations. In the contact mutant R273H, the ligand stabilized the DNA-binding interface while maintaining favorable conformational dynamics without introducing steric clashes. DISCUSSION: ADMET profiling predicts high bioavailability and a non-toxic safety profile, characterizing Hydroxymycotrienin A as a promising, bioavailable 'privileged scaffold' that offers a non-covalent therapeutic strategy for NSCLC. By restoring p53 function, this study addresses Sustainable Development Goals Target 3.4 to reduce premature mortality from non-communicable diseases. However, future in vitro and in vivo studies are required to validate the efficacy of these compounds.
abstract_zh: 引言：非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）中的TP53突变仍是一个严峻的临床挑战。当前使用共价结合剂APR-246的策略受限于脱靶毒性和耐药性。方法：本研究筛选了1,580种芽孢杆菌来源的代谢物，以识别针对天然、构象突变型（R175H）和接触突变型（R273H）p53的新型非共价药理学伴侣。通过虚拟筛选、ADMET分析、分子对接、延长至500 ns的分子动力学（Molecular Dynamics, MD）模拟及主成分分析，与实验性抗癌药物APR-246及排名靠前的化合物进行比较。结果：Hydroxymycotrienin A成为潜在候选物，表现出热力学优越性，对R175H和R273H的结合亲和力分别为-6.63 kcal/mol和-6.57 kcal/mol，在突变p53蛋白中显示出显著优于APR-246母体骨架（约-3.5 kcal/mol）的非共价对接亲和力，提示其具有直接的药理学伴侣活性。与APR-246的共价烷基化机制不同，Hydroxymycotrienin A利用非共价网络来伴侣突变型p53。MD模拟揭示，Hydroxymycotrienin A通过抑制L2环内的原子波动并减少整体结构偏差，作为构象突变型R175H的结构稳定剂。在接触突变型R273H中，配体稳定了DNA结合界面，同时保持有利的构象动态，未引入空间位阻。讨论：ADMET分析预测其具有高生物利用度和无毒安全性特征，将Hydroxymycotrienin A定性为一种有前景、可生物利用的“特权骨架”，为非小细胞肺癌提供了一种非共价治疗策略。通过恢复p53功能，本研究响应可持续发展目标3.4，旨在降低非传染性疾病导致的过早死亡率。然而，未来仍需进行体外和体内研究以验证这些化合物的有效性。
